title: Hopper FP8 operational failsafe and robustness playbook (E4M3/E5M2 per-shard selection)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Ship a robust operational playbook and runtime implementation to enable FP8 on Hopper GPUs across production workloads. This ticket covers the combination of per-shard E4M3/E5M2 selection heuristics, runtime safety checks, deterministic fallback paths, enhanced calibration workflows, and the observability and canary gating required for safe rollout. We must ensure accuracy regressions are within acceptable bounds, avoid silent degradation for tail customers, and provide clear rollback and mitigation steps for incidents.
reproduction_steps: 1. Run the FP8 calibration pipeline against the onboarding evaluation set (LLM-evals + customer prompts) using the current per-layer calibration config.
2. Execute inference on a Hopper E4M3/E5M2 cluster with synthetic and production-like traces (varying sequence lengths: 32, 256, 1024) capturing per-shard quantization choices.
3. Inject controlled noise/drift into activations (scale biases + random 0.5-1.5x) to validate per-shard selector stability and check fallback triggers.

4. Run end-to-end regression tests comparing FP8 output distributions against FP16 baseline for the eval prompts and compute automated quality metrics (perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE proxies, token-level edit rates).
5. Perform a small canary in production with traffic shadowing and compare live latency/cost metrics and customer-facing output diffs.
6. If any threshold breach occurs (see acceptance_criteria), trigger rollback to INT8/FP16 path and create an incident record.
acceptance_criteria: Accuracy: end-to-end eval on representative prompt set shows <= 0.25% mean metric regression (or configurable per-model SLAs) compared to FP16 baseline.
Stability: <0.5% of requests across canary cohort should have per-token divergence > threshold (configurable) attributable to quantization instability.
Telemetry: New metrics emitted and visible in Console: per-shard selector rate (E4M3 vs E5M2), fallback_count, calibration_drift_score, per-model accuracy_delta; alerts configured.
Fallbacks: Runtime implements deterministic fallback for any per-shard selector anomaly and end-to-end fallback to INT8/FP16 within 200ms of detection.
CI gating: Unit and integration tests added to calibration pipeline and runtime CI so PRs that touch selector logic must pass golden-case accuracy checks and stress tests.
Rollout: Canary with 1% traffic for 48 hours with automated quality and latency gates before 10% and 100% rollouts.
Runbook: On-call playbook documented with triage steps, key dashboards, and postmortem template for FP8 incidents.
design_notes: Per-shard selection should prefer E4M3 for layers with narrow dynamic range and E5M2 for high-dynamic-range activations; selection is informed by activation distribution stats captured during calibration.
Selector must be lightweight: use precomputed per-layer histograms + a simple scoring function rather than an expensive per-request model.
Introduce a safety band: if calibration confidence < threshold, mark layer as 'unstable' and force E5M2 or fallback to INT8 depending on risk profile.
Avoid runtime non-determinism by pinning RNG seeds in calibration runs and recording selection choices in model metadata to enable reproducible rollbacks.
We prefer observable heuristics instead of ML-based selectors initially to simplify audits and debugging.
Keep the decision surface coarse-grained initially (per-shard/per-layer), and iterate to sub-layer granularity only if empirically needed.
testing_plan: Calibration CI: add golden calibration artifacts and a regression harness that verifies calibration outputs are stable across commits.
Stress tests: batch/streaming concurrency tests to ensure selector codepath does not add >2ms median latency overhead at 95th percentile load.
Canary plan: 1% shadowed traffic for 48h (functional), then 1% live traffic with abort-on-quality-drop for next 48h.
A/B metrics: compare FP8 canary vs FP16 baseline on latency, cost-per-token, and quality delta; automate daily snapshot diffs.
Synthetic drift tests: script that monotonically changes activation scales and verifies fallback triggers and that no silent failures occur.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dev cluster test (dev-green) with calibration artifacts applied to a small model.
Stage 1: QA cluster integration test with full telemetry enabled and simulated production load.
Stage 2: Shadow canary (no user-facing traffic) for 72 hours comparing outputs and telemetry.
Stage 3: 1% live canary with automated gates (accuracy, latency, fallback rate) for 48 hours.
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% if metrics stable; full rollout after 7-day health window.
If any gate is tripped: abort rollout, flip runtime flag to force INT8/FP16, open incident, run postmortem.
